For the architecture actually trained this holds verbatim as long as 𝔼⁡[β⁡(X)∣YI]\mathbb{E}[\beta(X)\mid Y_{I}] lies in ran(A)\range(A), which is expected here because AA maps 130 321130\,321 pixels to 46 20846\,208 measurements and is therefore expected to have full row rank; otherwise the target is the L2L^{2}-projection of 𝔼⁡[A​X+β⁡(X)∣YI]\mathbb{E}[AX+\beta(X)\mid Y_{I}] onto the realized class, and the deviation from 𝔼⁡[A​X∣YI]\mathbb{E}[AX\mid Y_{I}] stays bounded by ‖𝔼⁡[β⁡(X)∣YI]‖\|\mathbb{E}[\beta(X)\mid Y_{I}]\|. The exactness is thus a property of (A4), which the pre-log Poisson model satisfies exactly and the count model (3.2) up to the bias just quantified; a bias-corrected target removes it entirely.

Both tasks use this same noisy acquisition model and differ only in the axis along which the input sinogram yIδy_{I}^{\delta} is subsampled:

  • •

    Detector Upscaling: the detector coordinate ss is subsampled with stride 44;

  • •

    Sparse-View Reconstruction: the angular coordinate θ\theta is subsampled with stride 44.

From subsampled data to full-size inputs:

Throughout Section 2.2, yIy_{I} is identified with its zero-embedding in ℝM\mathbb{R}^{M}. In the implementation we replace zero-filling by a linear extension operator E:ℝI→ℝME\colon\mathbb{R}^{I}\to\mathbb{R}^{M}, which interpolates linearly along the subsampled axis (ss for detector upscaling, θ\theta for sparse-view reconstruction). The initial reconstruction is x0=B⁡(E⁡(yIδ))x^{0}=B\bigl(E(y_{I}^{\delta})\bigr) with BB the filtered backprojection. Hence B∘EB\circ E plays the role of the initial reconstruction map BIB_{I} in Condition 2.22. Since BI=B∘EB_{I}=B\circ E, the intertwining requirement of Condition 2.18.2 must be verified for EE as well as for BB. It holds: the retained index sets are the stride-44 lattices {0,4,…,124}\{0,4,\dots,124\} in θ\theta and {0,4,…,360}\{0,4,\dots,360\} in ss, and both are invariant under the index maps induced by D4D_{4}, namely the angular shift by 6464 grid points (a rotation by π/2\pi/2 on the grid θj=j​π/128\theta_{j}=j\pi/128), the angular reversal j↦128−jj\mapsto 128-j and the detector reversal i↦360−ii\mapsto 360-i, because 128128 and 360360 are divisible by 44. Linear interpolation along a subsampled axis uses a symmetric two-point stencil with weights depending only on the distance to the neighbouring retained indices, and these distances are preserved by shifts and reversals of the lattice; hence EE commutes with the induced permutations and E∘Tℓ=Tℓ∘EE\circ T_{\ell}=T_{\ell}\circ E on ℝI\mathbb{R}^{I}. Combined with B​Tℓ=Sℓ​BBT_{\ell}=S_{\ell}B this gives BI​Tℓ=Sℓ​BIB_{I}T_{\ell}=S_{\ell}B_{I}. As discussed in Remark 2.27, FBP-based maps are not least-squares right-inverses of PI∘AP_{I}\circ A (not even right-inverses in the standard sense), so Condition 2.22.1 is satisfied only approximately in our experiments; the results below indicate that the method is robust with respect to this violation.

Supervision mask PSP_{S}:

The supervision set SS selects one quarter of the projection angles and one half of the detector bins,

S=Θ0×S0,Θ0={θ:θ∈[0,π/4)},S0={s:s≥0},S=\Theta_{0}\times S_{0},\qquad\Theta_{0}=\{\theta:\theta\in[0,\pi/4)\},\qquad S_{0}=\{s:s\geq 0\},

covering an area fraction of |S|/(Nθ​Ns)=(32/128)×(181/361)≈1/8|S|/(N_{\theta}N_{s})=(32/128)\times(181/361)\approx 1/8 of the sinogram, and the transformed sets {Tℓ​(S)}ℓ=18\{T_{\ell}(S)\}_{\ell=1}^{8} cover the sinogram grid up to the exceptional set determined below.

Coverage of the supervision set:

On the discrete grid, the covering by {Tℓ​(S)}ℓ=18\{T_{\ell}(S)\}_{\ell=1}^{8} is not exactly one-to-one, because the D4D_{4}-action has fixed points. This is visible already at the level of cardinalities: 8​|S|=8⋅32⋅181=46 3368\,|S|=8\cdot 32\cdot 181=46\,336, whereas the grid has Nθ​Ns=128⋅361=46 208N_{\theta}N_{s}=128\cdot 361=46\,208 points. Writing

n⁡(θ,s):=#⁡{ℓ:(θ,s)∈Tℓ​(S)},∑ℓ=18‖PS​Tℓ​v‖22=∑θ,sn⁡(θ,s)​vθ,s2,n(\theta,s):=\#\{\ell:(\theta,s)\in T_{\ell}(S)\},\qquad\sum_{\ell=1}^{8}\|P_{S}T_{\ell}v\|_{2}^{2}=\sum_{\theta,s}n(\theta,s)\,v_{\theta,s}^{2},

an explicit evaluation of the eight permutations gives n≡1n\equiv 1 on 96.6%96.6\% of the grid, together with the following exceptional set: the two projection angles θ∈{0,π/2}\theta\in\{0,\pi/2\} and the central detector column s=0s=0 are covered twice, and their intersection four times, because they are fixed by a reflection; the orbit θ∈{π/4,3​π/4}\theta\in\{\pi/4,3\pi/4\} is not covered at all, because it is disjoint from the half-open sector Θ0=[0,π/4)\Theta_{0}=[0,\pi/4), and on those two lines s=0s=0 is of course not covered either. Explicitly, n≡1n\equiv 1 on 44 64044\,640 coordinates, n=2n=2 on 844844, n=4n=4 on 22 and n=0n=0 on 722722, which sums to 8​|S|=46 3368\,|S|=46\,336. Condition (A7) therefore holds in the approximate form (2.2) with c1=1c_{1}=1, c2=4c_{2}=4 and QQ the coordinate projection onto the complement of the two uncovered angular lines. Theorem 2.17 applies with c1=1c_{1}=1 and therefore identifies 𝔼⁡[A​X∣YI]\mathbb{E}[AX\mid Y_{I}] exactly on the range of QQ, that is on 45 48645\,486 of the 46 20846\,208 sinogram coordinates, or 98.4%98.4\%; the uneven multiplicities on the fixed lines reweight the risk but do not move its minimizer. On the two uncovered angular lines the masked risk is entirely unconstrained, so whatever accuracy is observed there is due to the hypothesis class rather than to the training criterion.

Figure 3.1 shows the eight images Tℓ​(S)T_{\ell}(S) together with the exceptional set. Up to that set they tile the sinogram domain, each point being covered exactly once; this is what (A7) asks for. Exact coverage is restored within the weighted formulation of Remark 2.16: taking the closed sector Θ0=[0,π/4]\Theta_{0}=[0,\pi/4] and the diagonal weight W(θ,s)=a⁡(θ)​b​(s)W_{(\theta,s)}=a(\theta)\,b(s) with a⁡(θ)=1/2a(\theta)=1/2 for θ∈{0,π/4}\theta\in\{0,\pi/4\} and a≡1a\equiv 1 otherwise, and b⁡(0)=1/2b(0)=1/2 and b≡1b\equiv 1 otherwise, one obtains ∑ℓ=18‖W1/2​PS​Tℓ​v‖22=‖v‖22\sum_{\ell=1}^{8}\|W^{1/2}P_{S}T_{\ell}v\|_{2}^{2}=\|v\|_{2}^{2} for every vv, i.e. (A7W) with c=1c=1. The experiments reported below use the unweighted mask PSP_{S} with the half-open sector; the two formulations differ on 3.4%3.4\% of the sinogram coordinates.

Verification of Condition 2.9:

Augmenting the training distribution by D4D_{4} makes it invariant by construction, so that Sℓ​X=dXS_{\ell}X\stackrel{{\scriptstyle d}}{{=}}X for ℓ=1,…,8\ell=1,\dots,8 holds exactly for the distribution the network is trained on, and Theorem 2.11 identifies the conditional expectation for that distribution. By the intertwining relation, Tℓ​A​X=A⁡(Sℓ​X)=dA​XT_{\ell}AX=A(S_{\ell}X)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle d}}{{=}}AX, so A​XAX is TℓT_{\ell}-invariant. Since each TℓT_{\ell} is a coordinate permutation and Poisson noise acts independently per coordinate, the Poisson corruption is conditionally equivariant, Tℓ​𝒫​(A​x)|A​x=d𝒫⁡(Tℓ​A​x)|Tℓ​A​xT_{\ell}\,\mathcal{P}(Ax)\ \big|\ Ax\ \stackrel{{\scriptstyle d}}{{=}}\ \mathcal{P}(T_{\ell}Ax)\ \big|\ T_{\ell}Ax. Moreover, the grid sizes Nθ=128N_{\theta}=128 and Ns=361N_{s}=361 are chosen such that the stride-44 subsampling lattice is preserved by the D4D_{4}-action, hence Tℓ​PI=PI​TℓT_{\ell}P_{I}=P_{I}T_{\ell}. Combining these properties yields

(Tℓ​yIδ,Tℓ​A​x)=d(yIδ,A​x),\bigl(T_{\ell}\,y_{I}^{\delta},\;T_{\ell}\,Ax\bigr)\ \stackrel{{\scriptstyle d}}{{=}}\ \bigl(y_{I}^{\delta},\;Ax\bigr),

i.e. the joint invariance (A6). The coverage condition (A7) holds with c=1c=1 in the weighted form (A7W), and in the approximate form (2.2) for the unweighted mask actually used.

What augmentation does and does not change:

Augmentation enforces (A6) rather than verifying it, and the two levels at which this matters should be separated. On the level of distributions, writing πX\pi_{X} for the law of the images in the data set and π¯X:=18​∑ℓ=18πSℓ​(X)\bar{\pi}_{X}:=\frac{1}{8}\sum_{\ell=1}^{8}\pi_{S_{\ell}(X)} for its D4D_{4}-symmetrization, the distribution the network is trained on is π¯X\bar{\pi}_{X}, so the results of Section 2.2 identify the conditional expectation under π¯X\bar{\pi}_{X}. If the underlying population is not D4D_{4}-invariant, and clinical CT images do have a canonical orientation, this need not coincide with the conditional expectation under πX\pi_{X}; evaluation on the original test images is therefore a generalization test beyond the invariance assumption rather than an instance of it.

On the level of the training objective, however, no such gap arises. Since the augmented training set is closed under the group action, Proposition 2.14 applies to each original image separately: for every equivariant candidate, the masked loss summed over the eight augmented copies of an image equals cc times the full, unmasked loss on that image. The empirical objective being minimized is thus exactly the full self-supervised empirical objective on the 358358 original images, up to the noise cross term that vanishes in the mean. Augmentation is therefore not a distortion of the training target but the finite mechanism that realizes the coverage condition; what it changes is the population to which the estimator is optimal.

Relation to the noise model:

The conditional independence of the two acquisitions is what brings the setup close to (A4); no Gaussian approximation of the Poisson statistics is used anywhere in the analysis.

What is satisfied only approximately is Condition 2.22: the FBP-based initial reconstruction is not a least-squares right-inverse of PI∘AP_{I}\circ A (Remark 2.27), and the noise decomposition 2.22.2 holds exactly for i.i.d. Gaussian rather than for Poisson noise. By Remark 2.33 this does not affect the correctness of the training criterion; it only means that 𝔼⁡[A​X∣YI]\mathbb{E}[AX\mid Y_{I}] need not lie in the realized hypothesis class, in which case training returns its best approximation therein. Together with the coverage defect quantified above, the experiments therefore serve as a robustness study for precisely those quantities that the theory identifies as the sources of approximation error: ELIPPS reaches, despite both violations, the same order of accuracy as the supervised reference model; the precise reading of that comparison is discussed in Section 3.6.

3.4 Implementation Details

All learned models use a U-Net backbone Φθ\Phi_{\theta} with base width 3232 and three down-/up-sampling stages. We train with Adam (learning rate 10−410^{-4}), gradient clipping ‖∇θℒ‖2≤1\|\nabla_{\theta}\mathcal{L}\|_{2}\leq 1, and batch size 88. Training runs for 10001000 epochs (20002000 for the ablation of Section 3.7), and the reported figures are those of the weights after the final epoch. No model selection is performed: the data set is split into training and test images only, so selecting a checkpoint by test performance would tune on the test set, and we therefore do not do it. Test evaluation is carried out every 1010 epochs for monitoring only.

Equivariant architecture:

Following Theorem 2.20, the reconstruction network is the D4D_{4}-symmetrized image-space network

fθ=18​∑ℓ=18Sℓ−1∘Φθ∘Sℓ,x^=fθ​(x0)=fθ​(B⁡(E⁡(yIδ))),f_{\theta}=\frac{1}{8}\sum_{\ell=1}^{8}S_{\ell}^{-1}\circ\Phi_{\theta}\circ S_{\ell},\qquad\hat{x}=f_{\theta}(x^{0})=f_{\theta}\bigl(B(E(y_{I}^{\delta}))\bigr),

which is 𝒮\mathcal{S}-equivariant by construction. Training minimizes the empirical counterpart of the partially self-supervised risk (2.5),

ℒ⁡(θ)=∑training pairs‖PS​A​fθ​(B⁡(E⁡(yIδ)))−ySδ‖22.\mathcal{L}(\theta)=\sum_{\text{training pairs}}\bigl\|P_{S}\,Af_{\theta}\bigl(B(E(y_{I}^{\delta}))\bigr)-y_{S}^{\delta}\bigr\|_{2}^{2}.

3.5 Compared Methods

No existing self-supervised method addresses the setting (1.2) with a fixed supervision set: full self-supervision requires measurements unavailable here, while sparse self-supervision and equivariant imaging use yIy_{I} alone and cannot exploit ySy_{S}. A direct comparison would either grant them data they cannot use or deprive ELIPPS of the data that defines its setting. We therefore compare against the reference points proper to this setting:

  1. 1.

    FBP: the model-based reconstruction xFBP=x0=B⁡(E⁡(yIδ))x^{\mathrm{FBP}}=x^{0}=B\bigl(E(y_{I}^{\delta})\bigr), followed by disk masking and clamping to [0,1][0,1].

  2. 2.

    Naive learned refinement: a plain (non-symmetrized) U-Net refinement of xFBPx^{\mathrm{FBP}}, trained with the masked sinogram loss ℒnaive​(θ)=∑‖PS​A​Φθ​(x0)−ySδ‖22\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{naive}}(\theta)=\sum\|P_{S}\,A\Phi_{\theta}(x^{0})-y_{S}^{\delta}\|_{2}^{2}, i.e., the same supervision data as ELIPPS but without equivariant symmetrization.

  3. 3.

    Naive learned refinement with D4D_{4} test-time augmentation: the same non-symmetrized network as in 2., but evaluated as 18​∑ℓSℓ−1​Φθ​(Sℓ​x0)\tfrac{1}{8}\sum_{\ell}S_{\ell}^{-1}\Phi_{\theta}(S_{\ell}x^{0}), i.e. averaged over the eight group elements at test time only. Since the symmetrized network fθf_{\theta} is simultaneously an eight-fold ensemble at inference, this baseline separates the effect of enforcing equivariance during training from the generic averaging that symmetrization also provides at test time.

  4. 4.

    Fully supervised reference: an oracle model trained with full clean sinograms (PS=IdP_{S}=\operatorname{Id}, noise-free targets), minimizing ∑‖A​Φθ​(x0)−A​x‖22\sum\|A\Phi_{\theta}(x^{0})-Ax\|_{2}^{2}. We call this model supervised for brevity; note that its targets are the clean full measurements A​xAx rather than ground-truth images, so in the taxonomy of Section 1 it is the full self-supervised oracle, which is the strongest reference available in the measurement domain.

It is a reference point, not an upper bound: optimization, architecture and sample size need not order the two models in either direction.

3.6 Results

Table 3.1 reports the quantitative performance on both tasks. The proposed equivariant model outperforms the naive refinement baseline by a wide margin and achieves performance close to that of the fully supervised model.

For detector upscaling, ELIPPS obtains 31.2631.26 dB PSNR and 0.8230.823 SSIM, compared with 31.4731.47 dB and 0.8270.827 for the supervised model. For sparse-view reconstruction, ELIPPS achieves 30.7930.79 dB PSNR and 0.8160.816 SSIM, compared with 31.0731.07 dB and 0.8200.820 for the supervised model. Thus, ELIPPS remains close to the fully supervised reference, with PSNR gaps of only 0.210.21 dB and 0.280.28 dB for detector upscaling and sparse-view reconstruction, respectively. The comparison with the test-time-augmented baseline separates the two mechanisms at work: averaging the naive model over the group at inference already gains 0.800.80 dB and 0.620.62 dB over the plain naive model, while enforcing equivariance during training adds a further 1.491.49 dB and 1.301.30 dB on top of that. The larger part of the margin is therefore due to the training criterion and not to the eight-fold ensemble that symmetrization also provides at test time. Supervision over only 1/81/8 of the sinogram, combined with the D4D_{4} symmetry, thus suffices to recover globally consistent measurements, in accordance with Theorem 2.11. These numbers establish the order of accuracy reached under partial self-supervision; they come from a single training run per configuration, so the comparison should be read at that resolution rather than as a ranking to within hundredths of a decibel.

The evolution of the test-set metrics over training is shown in Figs. 3.2 and 3.3. For both tasks, ELIPPS consistently outperforms the naive learned baseline and approaches the fully supervised reference. The curves also show that the reported final-epoch values are representative of the performance reached near the end of training.

Figure 3.4 shows qualitative comparisons: relative to FBP and naive refinement, ELIPPS produces fewer artifacts and sharper structures.

3.7 Ablation Study: Effect of D4D_{4} Data Augmentation

The theory of Section 2.2 requires the D4D_{4}-invariance of the data distribution, which we enforced above by explicit D4D_{4} augmentation. To assess the role of this augmentation, we repeat the training on the same 1%1\% LoDoPaB subset without D4D_{4} augmentation. In this setting, the invariance assumption (A6) is no longer enforced exactly, and the network must rely on the architectural equivariance and the physics-driven loss alone to generalize across unobserved regions. Training runs for 20002000 epochs and test evaluation is performed every 1010 epochs. The budget therefore differs from the 10001000 epochs used for the main results, so the two tables are not a like-for-like comparison; the ablation should be read as evidence that the architectural prior remains effective without symmetry-balanced data, not as a measurement of the size of the effect.

Performance remains stable (Table 3.2): relative to the D4D_{4}-augmented setting ELIPPS loses 0.520.52 dB for detector upscaling and 0.810.81 dB for sparse-view reconstruction, with gaps to the reference of 0.190.19 and 0.440.44 dB, while still outperforming the naive baseline by a wide margin. Architectural equivariance therefore acts as a regularizer even when the training data are not symmetry-balanced.

Figures 3.5 and 3.6 qualify these numbers. Without augmentation the ELIPPS curves peak at roughly 900900 to 12001200 epochs and then decline slowly, whereas the reference stays flat, so the fixed budget of 20002000 epochs lies past the maximum and part of the gap above follows from the budget rather than from the method. We report the final-epoch value nonetheless, since with no validation set selecting the peak would be selection on the test set. We do not interpret the decline: these are single runs on 358358 images, and ordinary overfitting is as plausible as any consequence of the violated (A6).

Figure 3.7 corroborates this: the equivariant model shows reduced aliasing and preserves structural detail.

3.8 Scope of the experimental study

Section 3 establishes a principle rather than a benchmark ranking: a reconstruction network can be trained from a fixed, incomplete supervision set alone and still reach the accuracy of a model trained with full clean measurements. The two instantiations were chosen so that this effect is visible rather than entangled with architecture search, and together with the reference points that bracket the setting they show that supervision on one eighth of the sinogram suffices.

We are not aware of another method that learns from partial self-supervision in the sense of (1.2), that is, from a supervision set that is fixed across acquisitions. Existing approaches either require ground-truth images or fully sampled measurements, or they learn from several distinct measurement operators [24], or from the undersampled measurement yIy_{I} alone, without any supervision set; the latter, including equivariant imaging and equivariant splitting, operate under the opposite requirement on the symmetry group discussed in Remark 2.19 and would, in the regime considered here, be deprived of the mechanism they rely on. A comparison with either family therefore answers a different question. The closest relative is [17], which the present framework generalizes from direct, noise-free observation to indirect, noisy and undersampled measurements.

Two aspects delimit what these numbers support. The study uses 358358 training and 3535 test images from a 1%1\% subset of LoDoPaB with one run per configuration, which fixes the resolution at which the comparison is meaningful; and the input and supervision sinograms come from two conditionally independent Poisson realizations, costing between 1.251.25 and 22 times the deployment scan depending on the task, so the protocol demonstrates the learning principle rather than a dose-neutral single-scan implementation, for which Poisson thinning is the natural variant.

Two properties of the construction are design principles rather than artefacts of this data set, and carry over to any modality whose forward operator intertwines with a finite symmetry group. The supervision set enters through its orbit, so what makes learning from one eighth of the measurements possible is the covering property of Proposition 2.15; SS is chosen by design and, by the same proposition, cannot be smaller, the eighth being attainable because the weighted mask makes the action effectively free. And since the training set is closed under the group action, Proposition 2.14 applies sample by sample: the masked loss minimized here is, for every equivariant candidate, the full unmasked loss on the original images.

4 Conclusion

We introduced ELIPPS, a self-supervised training paradigm for undersampled inverse problems that requires neither ground-truth images nor fully sampled measurements: training uses only undersampled inputs together with incomplete measurements on a fixed supervision set. Two structural properties render this seemingly ill-posed problem well-posed, invariance of the data distribution under a family of transformations and intertwining of these transformations with the forward operator. Over the induced equivariant class the partially self-supervised risk is proportional to the full self-supervised risk, equivariance can be enforced architecturally at no cost when the initial reconstruction is a least-squares right-inverse of the subsampled forward operator, and the minimizer over the trained architecture class is the conditional expectation, which in the image domain is the minimum mean squared error estimator up to ker⁡(A)\ker(A). Over an arbitrary equivariant class the two risks have the same minimizers, so misspecification causes an approximation error but never an inconsistent training target; and uneven coverage leaves the conditional expectation identified exactly wherever the transformed supervision sets reach at all. For CT with the dihedral group D4D_{4}, supervision on one eighth of the sinogram brings both detector upscaling and sparse-view reconstruction to the same order of accuracy as a reference model trained on full clean measurements.

Several directions remain. The equivalence of the two risks requires only conditionally centered supervision noise, which covers pre-log Poisson statistics exactly and the log-transformed count model up to a quantifiable bias; the analysis of the factorized architecture, in contrast, uses an independence structure that is exact only for i.i.d. Gaussian noise, and the FBP is not a least-squares right-inverse. Quantitative estimates for approximate right-inverses and for approximate independence are an open question. The conditional centering is also what forces the two acquisitions, and blind-spot architectures achieve the same independence from a single measurement, at the price of a network constraint that would have to be made compatible with the equivariance imposed here. Further directions include nonlinear forward operators, learned initial reconstructions, continuous symmetry groups, and other modalities such as magnetic resonance imaging or photoacoustic tomography.
